t: You're on Great Cumberland Place, a street in the City of Westminster. Not much is recorded about the street itself, but several people with grand connections were born here. Frederick Gordon-Lennox, the ninth Duke of Richmond, was a racing driver and motor racing promoter, who went on to found the Goodwood Circuit on his Sussex estate. George Murray, the sixth Duke of Atholl, was a Scottish peer, important landowner and freemason. Alfred Walter Bagot, born in 1816, and Hubert Foljambe, born in 1872, were also born here.
